run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T14:02:25Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing because the proxy returns HTTP 503 on a small but persistent fraction of requests. In the frontend-proxy access log the failing requests carry response flag UC with code detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}, upstream cluster 'frontend' — i.e. the frontend upstream closed the connection before sending response headers. Span metrics confirm the errors sit only on frontend-proxy's 'ingress' operation (the paired 'router frontend egress' operation has 0 error spans) and are steady at roughly 5–9 error spans per 10 minutes across ~13:25–14:06. The frontend workload itself looks healthy at the infrastructure and telemetry level: single Ready pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 with 0 restarts, single Service endpoint 100.96.2.93, no crash/Kill/OOM events, no error spans of its own, and stable p95/p99 span latency; so the observable failure mode is connection termination by the frontend upstream, while the internal application reason could not be verified because the frontend container's logs were unreadable and no container CPU/memory/restart metrics exist in this Prometheus. A mid-window load-generator rollout at 13:53 is a change to the client, not the cause (frontend-proxy errors predate it).

claims.text: frontend-proxy has error spans only on operation 'ingress' (status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR): 1h increase reads 17.31 rising to 20.29 across the returned points, while operation 'router frontend egress' shows 0 error increase for every point and both operations carry ~20k–24.8k STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans.

Per-service error-span increases (10m range) show frontend-proxy as the only service whose errors rise in the window: 0 at the first points, then 1.07, 3.16, 6.32, 8.48, 9.47 (peak), settling at ~5.3 error spans per 10m. ad, fraud-detection and recommendation hold a constant ~1.05 per 10m on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream spans, and frontend shows 0.

The only frontend-proxy operation with error spans is 'ingress'; in the same per-operation query, frontend's own operations (GET, POST, executing api route (pages) /*, grpc.oteldemo.*) all read 0 errors, as do product-catalog, cart, checkout, currency, shipping, quote, email and accounting series returned.

frontend-proxy access logs show HTTP 503 responses with response flag UC and code detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}, upstream cluster 'frontend' (upstream host 100.71.53.109:8080, the frontend Service address). Ten such lines occur between 13:52:14 and 14:06:04 on GET /api/recommendations, GET /api/data/, GET /api/cart and GET /api/products/*. In the same read (11,307 lines, 13:50:25–14:12:15) these were the only 4xx/5xx lines; everything else was 200 or 308.

Successful requests to the same paths and from the same client are interleaved with the 503s: lines at 13:52:21–13:52:24 show 200 via_upstream for /api/recommendations, /api/products/*, /api/cart and /api/checkout and 308 for /api/data/?contextKeys=*, so the proxy routing itself works and only a minority of requests is reset.

frontend and frontend-proxy deployments are both 1/1 desired/available/ready/updated on images ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend and ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend-proxy; their pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 (frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2, frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4dlth).

The frontend Service has exactly one endpoint, 100.96.2.93:8080, matching pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 (pod IP 100.96.2.93, created 2026-11-16T13:21:27Z); no stale or duplicate frontend endpoint is present.

All 21 otel-demo pods were created 13:21:25–13:23:08 (flagd at 13:23:08), so the 13:21 frontend/frontend-proxy pod ages are a namespace-wide (re)start of the demo stack, not a frontend-specific change during the incident.

The only Kubernetes events in otel-demo inside the window are a load-generator rollout at 13:53:15–13:53:16: ScalingReplicaSet load-generator scaled up replica set load-generator-84895ffcd 0→1 and scaled down load-generator-57ffcd644 1→0, pod load-generator-57ffcd644-8ft89 deleted ('Stopping container load-generator') and load-generator-84895ffcd-hp7pb created/started. No Kill, Evicted, OOM or Unhealthy event exists for frontend or frontend-proxy.

frontend workload latency shows no rising trend inside the available data: p95 span duration is 185–289 ms and p99 is 576–739 ms at 5-minute steps from 13:27 to 14:07, and frontend-proxy 'ingress' p95 (histogram estimate) stays in 492–701 ms across 13:02–14:11.

A whole-service span ratio computed as sum(rate(error spans[5m])) / sum(rate(all spans[5m])) for frontend-proxy never exceeds ~0.00126 (peak at 13:38) and is 0 at the first points and at 14:12; it never reaches the 0.0111 stated in the alert annotation, so the alert's exact expression is not reproduced by this service-wide span ratio.

Resource limits for the two workloads are very small: frontend container limits cpu 100m / memory 200Mi (requests 50m/100Mi) and frontend-proxy container limits cpu 30m / memory 50Mi (requests 15m/25Mi); no readiness/liveness probes are defined on either container.

The 503s originate in the frontend application process: the frontend (a single Ready pod with no restarts, no crash events and no error spans of its own) closes upstream connections before response headers. This is what the proxy's UC / upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} detail on upstream cluster 'frontend' records, but the app-level reason inside the frontend container cannot be confirmed with the available data.

A connection-lifecycle mismatch between frontend-proxy's upstream pool and the frontend HTTP server (Envoy reusing/expecting a connection that the frontend closes) would produce exactly this sporadic pattern — a steady ~0.5–1% of interleaved, otherwise successful requests flagged UC with connection_termination, independent of load — but the proxy's Envoy configuration is baked into the image (no otel-demo ConfigMap holds it) and could not be inspected here.

Resource starvation could contribute: frontend-proxy is limited to 30m CPU and frontend to 100m CPU / 200Mi memory, which can cause event-loop/scheduling delays on either side. No container CPU, throttling or memory series exist in this Prometheus, so the hypothesis is untested rather than supported.

The 13:53 load-generator rollout is not the cause: frontend-proxy ingress error spans are already present well before 13:53 (per-10m error increases of 3.16 at the 13:29 point, 8.42 at 13:34 and peaks of 9.47 at 13:32), and the rollout only replaced the client pod load-generator-57ffcd644-8ft89 with load-generator-84895ffcd-hp7pb with the same image already present on the node.

A failing dependency does not explain the 503s: frontend reports no error spans on any gRPC/HTTP operation, product-catalog p95 is flat at ~1.92 ms, cart 51–99 ms and recommendation 29–85 ms with no upward trend, and the residual error spans on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation are flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream spans at a constant ~1 per 10m across the whole window (present before the frontend-proxy errors).

The frontend pod was not damaged or rolled out separately: it is the only frontend pod, Ready, restartCount 0, created together with all 21 demo pods at 13:21:25–13:21:27, and the Service has one matching endpoint; no probe or scheduling failure event was recorded for it.

Read the frontend container's stdout/stderr directly (kubectl logs, including any Node.js unhandledRejection/socket error text) for 13:45–14:10, and compare frontend-proxy's Envoy upstream connection settings (idle timeout / keepalive) against the frontend server's keep-alive timeout, since the current evidence locates the reset at the frontend upstream but cannot show why the frontend closed the connections.

gaps: Frontend container logs could not be read at all (fetch_pod_logs returned 0 lines / status no_data for frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 over 13:02:25–14:12:15), so the application-level reason the frontend terminated these connections is unknown; no 'previous' container instance exists either, so no restart evidence there.

This Prometheus has no kube-state-metrics series: get_metric_names for {__name__=~"kube_.*"} returned no data, so pod restart counts, CPU throttling and memory usage of frontend/frontend-proxy cannot be verified over time, and only point-in-time Kubernetes objects are available.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so whether frontend/frontend-proxy configuration or images changed cannot be verified.

Traces span-metric series only have samples in roughly the last hour of the window (a 24h range query returned a single evaluation point), so no baseline older than ~13:12 exists for any latency or error comparison.

Jaeger returned no trace for the failing requests: searches for frontend-proxy spans tagged http.status_code="503", otel.status_code="ERROR" and error="true" in 13:45–14:12 returned no traces, and a frontend search for 13:51–13:52:30 returned none, so the frontend-side spans of the reset requests could not be inspected.

The exact alerting expression behind the reported value 0.01111111111111111 is unknown; a service-wide error/all-span ratio for frontend-proxy peaks at ~0.00126, so the alert's metric cannot be reproduced from the visible span metrics alone.

Access-log reads stopped at 14:07:11 (read limit) and the earlier read reached only 13:50:24, so 503 occurrences before 13:50 and after 14:07 were not observed; the true count of reset requests in the window is unknown.
next_steps: Collect frontend container logs (kubectl logs -p included) for 13:45–14:10 to find the application error or socket termination that precedes each 503.
Inspect frontend-proxy's effective Envoy configuration (upstream keepalive/idle timeouts, max requests per connection) and compare it with the frontend HTTP server's keep-alive timeout.
Check frontend and frontend-proxy CPU throttling / memory usage (container metrics, cgroup throttle counters) against their 100m/200Mi and 30m/50Mi limits.
Confirm the alerting rule's exact PromQL to reconcile the reported 0.0111 with the observed ~0.0013 error-span ratio and to see which span operation/labels the rule aggregates.
